summary:
Good morning, everyone!

Welcome to a journey through the forgotten history of space exploration!

For the NASA challenge, inspired by the theme **"Abandoned but Not Forgotten,"** we didn't just collect information; we brought forgotten space missions back to life.

Throughout history, humanity has sent remarkable spacecraft to explore the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Yet, many of these missions have gradually disappeared from public attention, despite their incredible achievements and contributions to science.

From **ALSEP**, which allowed scientists to continue studying the Moon, to **Viking, Phoenix, and InSight**, which helped us explore Mars, and from **NEAR Shoemaker** to **Pioneer 10 and 11 and Dawn**, every mission has a story worth telling.

But how can we make these stories reach people again?

We created an educational website that brings these missions together, presenting their journeys, discoveries, and achievements. We also developed an interactive game for children, transforming space exploration into an enjoyable learning experience.

Our mission is simple: to reconnect people with humanity's forgotten achievements, inspire curiosity in younger generations, and prove that a spacecraft may stop operating, but its legacy never truly disappears.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

​Our project is an interactive platform dedicated to exploring "forgotten" or lesser-known NASA space missions, spacecraft, and artifacts. It works through a user-friendly website that features detailed historical timelines (launch and landing dates), precise specifications like dimensions and sizes, and immersive 3D models. Additionally, it includes an educational mini-game designed specifically for children to make learning about space history fun and engaging.

​What benefits does it have?

​It rescues important pieces of space history from being forgotten, turning them into accessible digital knowledge. For children and students, the interactive 3D models and educational game simplify complex aerospace concepts, fostering curiosity in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields.

​What is the intended impact of the project?

​The intended impact is to spark a lifelong interest in space exploration and science among the younger generation. By highlighting historical missions that laid the groundwork for modern space exploration, we aim to educate the public and preserve aerospace heritage in an entertaining, digital-first format.

​What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

​We utilized web development languages (such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript) to build the website. For the 3D models and interactive elements, we used specialized graphics tools and libraries (like Three.js or Blender), alongside game development tools to create the kids' educational game.

​How is your project creative?

​Our project stands out by combining historical archiving with modern interactive technology. Instead of a traditional text-based database, we brought forgotten space missions back to life using 3D visualization and gamification, turning passive reading into an active, playful learning adventure.

​What factors did your team consider?

​Our team carefully considered user experience (UX) and age-appropriate design, ensuring the platform is intuitive and engaging for children. We also prioritized historical accuracy by verifying launch/landing dates and vehicle specifications, alongside optimizing website performance for smooth 3D rendering.
